The test image shows a broken/split corn stalk with:
- Small black dots scattered on the tan/brown stalk surface
- Shredded/disintegrated pith tissue
- Tan-brown coloration throughout
- Stalk collapse/lodging

Top candidates: **Diplodia_stalk_rot** (small black pycnidia + shredded pith), **Charcoal_stalk_rot** (tiny black sclerotia + shredded pith), **Anthracnose_stalk_rot** (shiny black rind + shredded pith).

Let me view reference images for all three simultaneously.
Now let me view 3 more reference images to meet the minimum requirement.

## Analysis

**Test image observations:**
- Close-up of a broken/split corn stalk at the lower internodes
- Numerous small black dots on the tan/brown stalk surface → **pycnidia**
- Shredded, fibrous pith tissue exposed at break point
- Tan-brown coloration (not gray/charcoal, not shiny black)
- Stalk collapse with lodging

**Comparison against candidates:**

| Feature | Test Image | Diplodia | Charcoal | Anthracnose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Black structures on stalk | Small dots (pycnidia) | ✅ Pycnidia | ✗ Microsclerotia (gray) | ✗ Shiny black rind blotches |
| Pith color | Tan/brown shredded | ✅ Tan/brown shredded | ✗ Gray/charcoal colored | ✗ Brown-black pith |
| Rind appearance | Tan/brown | ✅ Tan/brown | ✗ Gray | ✗ Shiny black streaks |

The small black pycnidia (pinhead-sized, cannot be scraped off) combined with shredded tan/brown pith in the lower internodes is the diagnostic combination for **Diplodia stalk rot**. The Diplodia reference collage (bottom-left panel) shows an almost identical view. Charcoal would show gray coloration throughout, and Anthracnose would show shiny black rind discoloration — neither matches.
